main_text.l: tio quærere, nihil aliud est, quàm contrà eius consilium superbire. Et Augustinus de Spiritu & litera, præclarè inquit: Operum Dei causa si lateat hominem, non sé obliuiscatur esse hominem, nec propterea Deo det insipientiam, quia non bene capit eius scientiam.
Hæc est inscriptio Psalmi Habacuc Prophetæ, quæ monet, inscitiam & infirmitatem nostram nobis potius esse confitendam, quàm cum Deo litigandum de eius operibus & iudiciis.
Rabi Salomon existimat, Prophetam voce Dei in hac disceptatione convictum erubuisse: & ut Deo debitam gloriam deferret, ignorantiam suam confessum esse.

Quod si vir tantus, patriæ excidium, hostium insolentiam, & alia mala publicè & privatim grassantia ingenti cum dolo re expertus & intues, cum primum à Domino admonitus, sese repressit, ac Deo gloriam dedit: meminerimus, idem nobis quoq; faciendum : rerum omnium[?]

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the heading line "ignorantiâ" is split at a line end ("ignô-" / "rantiâ") and is partly unclear; the final letters of "omnium" appear as a contracted form (omniū?) and are uncertain. The catchword "ini" is uncertain. The signature "t 3" and the first fragment "tio" are kept as printed. "dolo re" is printed without a hyphen across the line break and is transcribed as printed. Long s has been normalised to s throughout.
